newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe industrial index ends at new record high.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe industrial index ends at new record high.

text.p: Zimbabwe's main industrial share index leapt over 66 points to a new record high on Tuesday in a market increasingly attractive to both long-term corporate investors and "overnight" speculative players, brokers said.
"Everyone who must be in is coming in, but the drivers are the institutions -- both local and foreign -- and the small guys looking for overnight gains," one broker said.
"They will all be in as long as everyone thinks things are going fine," he said of the Zimbabwe Stock Exchange which is expected to remain bullish for at least the next three months.
This is based on predictions that the southern African country's agriculture-based economy will grow by seven percent in 1997 if current heavy rains continue.

Brokers said investors descended on industrials across the board, but they singled out gains in heavyweights Zimbabwe Sugar Refinery (ZSR), 25 cents up at 1,400, banking group Barclays, 50 cents higher at 2,350, and conglomerate Delta, also 50 cents up at 3,400, as the power behind the industrial index's jump.
The 57-counter industrial index, which lost over 55 points on Monday, bounced back 66.07 points to close at a record 8,127.83.
The secondary seven-share mining index climbed 4.20 points to 1,201.07 following a 15 cents rise in coal producer Wankie at 430.
But brokers said trade in minings continued generally quiet as a majority of investors ploughed their money into industrial counters.
